1: ---
2: name: rigorous-proof
3: description: Use Yui to make an existing mathematical proof self-contained as structured NL0 with Audit A, then optionally translate it through typed interfaces into Lean with source-faithful Audit B. Supports NL0-only, translation from an accepted NL0, and full workflows. Do not infer proof correctness from schema checks or introduce unproved assumptions to close a goal.
4: ---
5: 
6: # Yui: rigorous proof development
7: 
8: Use the smallest requested track. Preserve the original problem, hypotheses,
9: definitions and proof route. The two stages share one specification and explicit
10: invalidation rules; completing stage one does not require stage two.
11: 
12: The installed skill root is the directory containing this `SKILL.md`. Keep
13: `config.json`, `nl0/`, `nl02lean/` and `toolchain/` beside it; no enclosing
14: `rigorous-proof/` subdirectory or particular checkout name is required.
15: 
16: ## Select a stage
17: 
18: Before dispatch, follow [target selection](nl0/references/target-selection.md).
19: Resolve a clear intended theorem yourself without asking again; ask the user
20: only when the intended target remains ambiguous. Freeze the complete selected
21: statement(s), including standing assumptions, as an explicit job input.
22: 
23: The invoking agent owns request/configuration collection and dispatch. Follow
24: [installed operation](nl0/references/operation.md) to identify explicit proof inputs,
25: ask once for missing active-phase model/reasoning/speed settings and, for a
26: NL0, full or translation request, an explicit per-case worker count N, then call
27: `nl0/scripts/yui.py run` (or prepare/execute). Retain settings already supplied by
28: the user; do not call a separate intent-classification model. Do not silently
29: choose a worker count from defaults or `auto`; obtain a positive integer or
30: the user's explicit confirmation of a proposed number. N bounds local R-node
31: reviews and, in a separate phase, local Lean proofs. NL0/Audit A and
32: Lean preparation/proofs/assembly/Audit B have separate phase profiles. The user
33: does not prepare queues, task packets or controller jobs manually.
34: The invoking owner follows [foreground handoff and monitoring](nl0/references/owner-observation.md):
35: normally dispatch with `--detach`, verify the owned processes, and register one
36: host heartbeat for a bounded check every ten minutes. Record the actual schedule
37: ID, report that mathematical work is still pending, then end the current
38: foreground turn. Never keep the owner active through sleep/poll loops. Each
39: scheduled check ends its turn as well. `DISPATCHED` is not workflow completion.
40: If host scheduling is unavailable, disclose that and return manual status/cancel
41: commands; do not claim that a monitor was registered. Frozen author/proof/reviewer
42: stages perform only their assigned roles and never schedule owner monitoring or
43: redispatch the workflow.
44: 
45: For missing external originals, follow [ordered source retrieval](nl0/references/source-retrieval.md):
46: arXiv, Google full-text search, Google DOI discovery, then confirmed-DOI Sci-Hub
47: lookup with ordinary browser readback when needed. Reuse an already available
48: adequate primary source; retrieval alone does not establish theorem fidelity.
49: At invocation disclose the [conditional-source policy](nl0/references/conditional-sources.md):
50: inaccessible primary texts can permit continued work from complete explicit
51: secondary statements, but the final result remains conditional. Show each
52: actual warning and include warn.json/warn.md in the final report. Never label
53: unverified sources or a qualified workflow as an ordinary full PASS.
54: 
55: Default permanent output is `<problem-directory>/rigorous-proof/<run-id>/`,
56: outside the installed skill. Multiple problems own separate outputs, contexts,
57: queues and ledgers. Use normal local repair unless a first-pass measurement is
58: explicitly requested. Runtime and software controls are fully inside this skill;
59: no repository example/support directory or old test result is required.
60: Positively identified temporary remote-service failures retry within the same
61: isolated thread, preserving its drafts and tool receipts. Keep the selected
62: profile and record every fault/wait; use [operational recovery](nl0/references/operation.md#remote-service-recovery)
63: for backoff, cancellation and explicit continuation of an already exited run.
64: 
65: 1. **NL0 and Audit A.** Use [Audit A's shared acceptance requirements](nl0/references/audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
66:    as the single mathematical standard for both author and auditor.
67:    Read [the NL0 stage](nl0/references/nl0-stage.md),
68:    [format](nl0/references/nl0-format.md), [self-containment](nl0/references/self-containment.md),
69:    [authoring](nl0/references/nl0-authoring.md), and Audit A's role-specific execution protocol.
70:    Read [external-source review](nl0/references/external-theorems.md) for citations
71:    and [logical packaging](nl0/references/logical-rules.md) for local assumptions.
72:    Use `nl0/scripts/nl0.py`; its explicit accounting is not a mathematical prover.
73:    Controllers and reviewers follow [completion and local repair](nl0/references/review-execution.md)
74:    for global-first parallel R coverage, exact evidence inheritance and stage boundaries.
75: 2. **Translate an accepted NL0 and run Audit B.** Verify the supplied Audit A
76:    authority and exact source version first; do not reconstruct or re-audit an
77:    unchanged proof. Start with [minimal translation](nl02lean/references/minimal-translation.md).
78:    Read [translation](nl02lean/references/stage.md),
79:    [the working sequence](nl02lean/references/integrated-workflow.md), and
80:    [Audit B](nl02lean/references/audit-b.md). Operators use
81:    [execution and file-based control](nl02lean/references/execution-protocol.md)
82:    for parallel queues, status and stops; workers need only their frozen packet.
83:    After local proofs complete, the serial postprocessing author follows
84:    [assembly and source-facing export](nl02lean/references/assembly.md),
85:    then hands actual checked evidence to a separate independent Audit B reviewer.
86:    Use
87:    `nl02lean/scripts/source_preparation.py` for bounded shared extraction,
88:    then `workflow.py` for source/IR freeze, proof work and final gates.
89: 3. **Full workflow.** Complete track one, then track two. A changed mathematical
90:    statement or new theorem returns to the affected NL0/Audit A boundary.
91: 
92: ## Mathematical invariants
93: 
94: - Accepted NL0 is a complete natural-language proof relative to explicit H/E/M,
95:   fixed logic and its hash-bound verified background supplement. Important
96:   tools remain explicit; ordinary correct elementary reasoning needs no
97:   exhaustive calculation chain. See [background notes](nl0/references/background-notes.md).
98: - Within NL0, each inference uses only its direct inputs, global definitions and explicitly
99:   established in-scope local facts or positively checked node-local background
100:   notes. Notes never add H or repair a substantive gap. Source papers and producer proof bodies do
101:   not fill gaps in a task packet.
102: - Preserve one global mathematical identity while allowing local Lean views.
103:   Actual cross-view conversions need checked proofs. In stage two, the pinned
104:   Mathlib environment is freely available without NL0 M registration.
105: - Shared mathematical extraction is a bounded local change at translation entry.
106:   Review its new producer and substitution cuts; inherit unchanged evidence.
107:   Freeze the revised NL0 before final IR and worker packets.
108: - Local conditional bodies may run concurrently. Assembly must discharge every
109:   internal dependency with an actual checked proof; conditional checks alone
110:   are not a final result.
111: - Audit B checks every external E and the complete target P, including its
112:   hypotheses, against actual Lean types and relevant definitions. Supply short
113:   direct/equivalent correspondence explanations; an independent reviewer verifies
114:   them. Check fresh Lean closure and trust, without a Mathlib-to-NL0 use ledger.
115:   Neither author notes nor a compiler pass are semantic approval.
116: - Stop on a judged substantive mathematical gap. Ordinary expansion and local
117:   verifiable corrections remain allowed. Difficulty or elapsed time does not
118:   establish that a mathematical claim is false.
119: 
120: ## Clean execution and accounting
121: 
122: Operators use [execution terminology](nl0/references/terminology.md) to distinguish
123: Codex conversations, native subagents, Yui jobs, worker slots and controllers.
124: Use the logical phase names **NL0 worker**, **preprocessing worker**,
125: **formalization workers (N slots)** and **postprocessing worker**. A logical
126: worker may contain several separate author/reviewer threads and program steps;
127: N limits concurrent local R reviews and local Lean proof jobs in their separate phases.
128: Report executor termination separately from mathematical acceptance.
129: 
130: Read [isolation](nl0/references/isolation.md) and [measurement](nl0/references/measurement.md)
131: before any model test or benchmark. Run model authoring, planning, proof and
132: review stages through the isolated carrier. The interactive developer's memory,
133: other personal skills, expert packages, old task outputs and hidden reference
134: proofs are never an input source for these stages.
135: 
136: The Yui arm receives only the declared Yui rules and task material. The direct
137: arm receives a minimal task/tool contract and the same mathematical inputs,
138: without Yui planning, strategy or shared-proof guidance. Log actual transmitted
139: instructions, complete allowed inputs, tool schemas/results, model identity,
140: phase, usage and health. Never execute model-generated Python or shell text.
141: 
142: Collect the active phase profiles as described above. `config.json` supplies
143: defaults only when explicitly selected. The current isolated carrier supports
144: Standard speed and checks model/effort availability without fallback. Freeze
145: and record each stage's selected profile;
146: never silently substitute a stronger model or fallback.
147: Resolve the confirmed concurrency before dispatch and record its basis; do not
148: claim an unknown backend maximum. N limits local R-node reviews, then local
149: Lean proof jobs in a later phase. NL0 authoring, global Audit A, preparation,
150: interface work, assembly and Audit B use one serial lane per case.
151: Count root/controller, worker, review and retry calls. Cached/reasoning tokens
152: are subsets of input/output totals, not extra tokens. Missing usage is unknown.
153: 
154: Return the exact accepted scope, source/formal artifacts, unresolved citations
155: or gaps, actual execution health, time/token breakdown, and reproducible commands.
156: Do not claim a universal NL0 compiler, an unconditional proof of literature
157: inputs, completed Audit C, or acceleration from this prototype alone.

1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.
183: 
184: ## Input status
185: 
186: This file fixes the exercise, notation and supplied proof, including the
187: arbitrary-lattice argument. It is not an NL0 artifact, an Audit A receipt,
188: a Lean proof, or a passing test result. Future runs must construct and check
189: those artifacts from these explicit inputs, registering any foundational
190: module or localization results used by their NL0.
